subproblems.title: Regularity and uniform bounds for a compact variation (Simon Ch. 4, 2.1)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), and let (φ, ε, K) be a compact variation as in Simon Ch. 4, 2.1 (IsCompactVariation φ ε K): ε > 0; K ⊆ E compact; (t, y) ↦ φ(t, y) is C^∞ on (−ε, ε) × E; for t ∈ (−ε, ε), φ_t := φ(t, ·) is bijective with C^∞ inverse Function.invFun φ_t; φ_0 = id; and φ_t(y) = y for t ∈ (−ε, ε), y ∉ K. Let X(y) := ∂_tφ(t, y)|_{t=0} (Lean: deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0). Then: (a) X is C¹; (b) DX(y) = 0 for every y ∉ K; (c) for every t ∈ (−ε, ε), φ_t is Lipschitz and C¹; (d) there are δ with 0 < δ < ε, B ∈ ℝ and Λ' : ℝ → E → L(E, E) such that for every x ∈ E: Λ'(0, x) = DX(x), and for every t ∈ (−δ, δ): s ↦ Dφ_s(x) has derivative Λ'(t, x) at s = t, ‖Dφ_t(x)‖ ≤ B, ‖Λ'(t, x)‖ ≤ B, and ‖v‖ ≤ B‖Dφ_t(x)v‖ for all v ∈ E.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 1 ("The variation", Simon Ch. 4, 2.1) together with step 3.1 (uniform bounds on [−ε/2, ε/2] × K), extended by the trivial bounds off K. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}; U := (−ε, ε) × E ⊆ ℝ × E; Φ(t, y) := φ t y; ι₁ := (1, 0) ∈ ℝ × E; ι₂ ∈ L(E, ℝ × E), ι₂v := (0, v) (ContinuousLinearMap.inr); X(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0; Dφ_t(y) := fderiv ℝ (φ t) y. The hypothesis IsCompactVariation φ ε K says: (H1) ε > 0; (H2) K is compact; (H3) Φ is C^∞ on U; (H4) for t ∈ (−ε, ε), φ t is bijective and Function.invFun (φ t) is C^∞; (H5) φ 0 y = y for all y; (H6) φ t y = y for t ∈ (−ε, ε) and y ∉ K. U is open (isOpen_Ioo.prod isOpen_univ).

1. Smoothness of DΦ. Since U is open and Φ is C^∞ on U, Φ is C^∞ at every q ∈ U (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt), hence differentiable there, and DΦ(q) := fderiv ℝ Φ q is C^∞ on U (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen); in particular DΦ is continuous on U and differentiable at every point of U.

2. Time slices. Fix t ∈ (−ε, ε). For every y ∈ E, (t, y) ∈ U, and φ t = Φ ∘ j_t with j_t(y) := (t, y), a C^∞ affine map whose derivative is ι₂. Hence φ t is C^∞ on E (composition of Φ, C^∞ on U, with j_t, which maps E into U), and by the chain rule Dφ_t(y) = DΦ(t, y) ∘ ι₂ =: G(t, y) for every y ∈ E. The map G(q) := DΦ(q) ∘ ι₂ is C^∞ on U, being DΦ followed by the fixed continuous linear map A ↦ A ∘ ι₂. In particular G is continuous on U and differentiable at every point of U.

3. Part (a). Fix y ∈ E. The map t ↦ (t, y) has derivative ι₁ and Φ is differentiable at (0, y) ∈ U, so t ↦ φ t y = Φ(t, y) has derivative DΦ(0, y)ι₁ at 0 (chain rule); hence X(y) = DΦ(0, y)ι₁. Therefore X = ev_{ι₁} ∘ DΦ ∘ k with k(y) := (0, y) (C^∞, k(E) ⊆ U) and ev_{ι₁}(A) := Aι₁ (continuous linear). As a composition of C^∞ maps, X is C^∞; in particular ContDiff ℝ 1 X.

4. Part (b). K is compact, hence closed, so W := E ∖ K is open. For y' ∈ W and t ∈ (−ε, ε), φ t y' = y' by (H6); thus t ↦ φ t y' is constant on the neighbourhood (−ε, ε) of 0, and X(y') = 0. So X vanishes on the open set W; for y ∈ W we get X =ᶠ[𝓝 y] 0, hence fderiv ℝ X y = fderiv ℝ 0 y = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).

5. Part (c). Fix t ∈ (−ε, ε). By step 2, φ t is C^∞, so ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t) and φ t is differentiable everywhere. For y ∈ W, φ t agrees with the identity on the open neighbourhood W of y (H6), so Dφ_t(y) = I and ‖Dφ_t(y)‖ ≤ 1. The map y ↦ Dφ_t(y) = G(t, y) is continuous, so it is bounded on the compact set K by some L₀ ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; any L₀ works if K = ∅). Hence ‖Dφ_t(y)‖ ≤ L := max(L₀, 1) for all y ∈ E, and the mean value inequality on the convex space E (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le) shows that φ t is Lipschitz with constant L (as an NNReal). This gives (∃ L, LipschitzWith L (φ t)) ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ t).

6. Invertibility of Dφ_t. Fix t ∈ (−ε, ε) and x ∈ E. Let ψ := Function.invFun (φ t); by (H4) ψ is C^∞, hence differentiable everywhere. As φ t is bijective, ψ(φ t y) = y and φ t (ψ y) = y for all y (Function.leftInverse_invFun, Function.rightInverse_invFun). Differentiating the first identity at x, and the second at y = φ t x (chain rule; note ψ(φ t x) = x), gives Dψ(φ t x) ∘ Dφ_t(x) = I and Dφ_t(x) ∘ Dψ(φ t x) = I. Hence G(t, x) = Dφ_t(x) is a unit of the normed ring L(E, E), with inverse Dψ(φ t x).

7. Definition of Λ'. Define Λ'(t, x) := (fderiv ℝ G (t, x)) ι₁ ∈ L(E, E) for all t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E. Let x ∈ E and t ∈ (−ε, ε). G is differentiable at (t, x) ∈ U (step 2) and s ↦ (s, x) has derivative ι₁, so s ↦ G(s, x) has derivative Λ'(t, x) at t. Since fderiv ℝ (φ s) x = G(s, x) for every s in the neighbourhood (−ε, ε) of t (step 2), HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq gives
(∗) HasDerivAt (s ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ s) x) (Λ'(t, x)) t for every x ∈ E and t ∈ (−ε, ε).
Moreover Λ' is continuous on U, since fderiv ℝ G is continuous on U (G is C^∞ on the open set U) and A ↦ Aι₁ is continuous linear.

8. Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x (symmetry of second derivatives). Fix x ∈ E and write D²Φ := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ) (0, x), so that (D²Φ a) b ∈ E for a, b ∈ ℝ × E.
(i) By step 3, X = ev_{ι₁} ∘ DΦ ∘ k with k(y) = (0, y), whose derivative is ι₂; DΦ is differentiable at k(x) = (0, x) ∈ U. By the chain rule, fderiv ℝ X x v = (D²Φ (ι₂ v)) ι₁ for v ∈ E.
(ii) G = (A ↦ A ∘ ι₂) ∘ DΦ on U, so fderiv ℝ G (0, x) a = (D²Φ a) ∘ ι₂ and hence Λ'(0, x) v = (D²Φ ι₁)(ι₂ v) for v ∈ E.
(iii) Φ is C^∞ at (0, x) ∈ U and minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2 ≤ ∞, so Φ has a symmetric second derivative at (0, x) (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt): (D²Φ a) b = (D²Φ b) a for all a, b. Taking a = ι₁, b = ι₂ v gives Λ'(0, x) v = fderiv ℝ X x v for all v, i.e. Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x.
Implementation note (not part of the argument): this step is available in the pinned library. For F(q) := φ q.1 q.2, which is C² at (0, x), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.Varifold.hasDerivAt_familySpatialDerivative together with familySpatialDerivative_eq_fderiv and initialVelocity_eq_deriv (there Euclidean N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) gives HasDerivAt (t ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ t) x) (fderiv ℝ X x) 0 after HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq; HasDerivAt.unique with (∗) at t = 0 then yields Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x.

9. Uniform bounds. Put δ := ε/2, so 0 < δ < ε, and Q := [−δ, δ] × K, a compact subset of U (compact × compact). On U the maps G (step 2), Λ' (step 7) and Inv(t, x) := Ring.inverse (G(t, x)) are continuous; the last because G(t, x) is a unit for (t, x) ∈ U (step 6) and Ring.inverse is continuous at every unit of a complete normed ring (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). By compactness there are B₁, B₂, B₃ ≥ 0 with ‖G‖ ≤ B₁, ‖Λ'‖ ≤ B₂ and ‖Inv‖ ≤ B₃ on Q (each bound may be taken 0 if K = ∅). Let B := max(1, max(B₁, max(B₂, B₃))).
(i) Let x ∈ K and t ∈ (−δ, δ). Then (t, x) ∈ Q, so ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x‖ = ‖G(t, x)‖ ≤ B and ‖Λ'(t, x)‖ ≤ B; and for v ∈ E, since Inv(t, x) ∘ G(t, x) = I (G(t, x) is a unit, Ring.inverse_unit), ‖v‖ = ‖Inv(t, x)(G(t, x) v)‖ ≤ B₃ ‖G(t, x) v‖ ≤ B ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x v‖.
(ii) Let x ∉ K and t ∈ (−δ, δ). For every s ∈ (−ε, ε), φ s agrees with the identity on the open neighbourhood W of x (H6), so fderiv ℝ (φ s) x = I. Hence ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x‖ = ‖I‖ ≤ 1 ≤ B and ‖v‖ = ‖I v‖ ≤ B ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x v‖ because B ≥ 1. The function s ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ s) x is constant (equal to I) on the neighbourhood (−ε, ε) of t, so it has derivative 0 at t; by (∗) and uniqueness of derivatives (HasDerivAt.unique), Λ'(t, x) = 0, and ‖Λ'(t, x)‖ = 0 ≤ B.

10. Conclusion. Parts (a), (b), (c) are steps 3, 4, 5. For (d) take δ and B from step 9 and Λ' from step 7: 0 < δ < ε; for every x ∈ E, Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x by step 8; and for every t ∈ (−δ, δ) ⊆ (−ε, ε), HasDerivAt (s ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ s) x) (Λ'(t, x)) t holds by (∗), and ‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x‖ ≤ B, ‖Λ'(t, x)‖ ≤ B and ‖v‖ ≤ B‖fderiv ℝ (φ t) x v‖ for all v hold by step 9. ∎
proof_key_steps: DΦ is C^∞ on the open set U = (−ε, ε) × E; Dφ_t(y) = G(t, y) := DΦ(t, y)∘ι₂ for t ∈ (−ε, ε), and X(y) = DΦ(0, y)(1, 0), so X is C^∞
X = 0 on the open set E ∖ K, hence DX = 0 off K
φ_t is C^∞ with Dφ_t = I off K and Dφ_t bounded on K, hence Lipschitz by the mean value inequality
Dφ_t(x) is invertible (chain rule on invFun φ_t ∘ φ_t = id and φ_t ∘ invFun φ_t = id); Λ'(t, x) := DG(t, x)(1, 0) is the t-derivative of Dφ_t(x)
Λ'(0, x) = DX(x) by symmetry of D²Φ(0, x) (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt)
Compactness of [−ε/2, ε/2] × K and continuity of G, Λ', Ring.inverse ∘ G give the bound B on K; off K, Dφ_t = I and Λ' = 0

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 2 ("Area formula on M", Simon Ch. 4, 1.5–1.6 and 2.2, with the area formula of Ch. 3 §2, 2.4–2.5), applied to a single injective Lipschitz map f in place of φ_t, together with the identity J^P(Λ)² = det S_P(Λ) from the parent's conventions. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ, N := n + ℓ, e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N), the standard orthonormal basis of E; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume); Hⁿ := μHE[n]. a = (M, θ) is an admissible pair (IsRectifiablePair: M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M); V := mk a, T_x := V.tangentSpace x. For a linear subspace P ⊆ E let p_P := P.starProjection (orthogonal projection onto P: self-adjoint, idempotent, identity on P, zero on P^⊥) and q_P := I − p_P (orthogonal projection onto P^⊥). For Λ ∈ L(E, E) put
S_P(Λ) := [⟨Λp_Pe_i, Λp_Pe_j⟩ + ⟨q_Pe_i, q_Pe_j⟩]_{i,j ∈ Fin N}, jac(Λ, P) := (det S_P(Λ))^{1/2} (Real.sqrt),
so the right-hand side of the claim is ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)) dHⁿ(x). Let J^P(Λ) := normDet(Λ|_P) ≥ 0, where Λ|_P := Λ ∘ ι_P : P → E (LinearMap.domRestrict) and normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet. For a map G: ℝⁿ → E, JG(v) := normDet(fderiv ℝ G v) (SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt). L denotes a Lipschitz constant of f, L_i one of F_i.

0. The tangential Jacobian: jac(Λ, P) = J^P(Λ) for every subspace P and every Λ ∈ L(E, E).
Let k := dim P and β(u, v) := ⟨Λp_Pu, Λp_Pv⟩ + ⟨q_Pu, q_Pv⟩, a bilinear form on E whose matrix in the basis (e_i) is S_P(Λ). Choose an orthonormal basis u_1, …, u_k of P and an orthonormal basis u_{k+1}, …, u_N of P^⊥; together they form an orthonormal basis of E. In this basis the matrix S^u := [β(u_a, u_b)]_{a,b} is block diagonal: for a, b ≤ k, β(u_a, u_b) = ⟨Λu_a, Λu_b⟩ (p_P = I and q_P = 0 on P); for a, b > k, β(u_a, u_b) = ⟨u_a, u_b⟩ = δ_{ab} (p_P = 0 and q_P = I on P^⊥); for a ≤ k < b or b ≤ k < a, β(u_a, u_b) = 0 (in each of the two summands one argument is killed). Hence det S^u = det[⟨Λu_a, Λu_b⟩]_{a,b≤k} = J^P(Λ)², by LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram applied to Λ|_P and the orthonormal basis (u_a)_{a≤k} of P (for k = 0 both sides are 1: the empty determinant, and LinearMap.normDet_of_subsingleton). Let O := [⟨e_i, u_a⟩]_{i,a}, an orthogonal matrix since both bases are orthonormal. From e_i = Σ_a ⟨e_i, u_a⟩u_a and bilinearity, S_P(Λ) = O S^u Oᵀ, so det S_P(Λ) = (det O)² det S^u = det S^u = J^P(Λ)². (Equivalently: S_P(Λ) and S^u are the matrices, in the orthonormal bases (e_i) and (u_a), of the operator p_PΛ*Λp_P + q_P, and the determinant of an operator does not depend on the basis, LinearMap.det_toMatrix.) Since J^P(Λ) ≥ 0, jac(Λ, P) = (J^P(Λ)²)^{1/2} = J^P(Λ).

1. Properties of f.
(a) f is injective, so Function.invFun f (f x) = x for all x (Function.leftInverse_invFun). Put u(y) := ofReal(θ(invFun f y)); then imageMass a f K = ∫⁻_{f(M∩K)} u dHⁿ and u(f(x)) = ofReal(θ(x)) for every x.
(b) For every Z ⊆ E, Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ L^n·Hⁿ(Z) (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn with A := Z); in particular f maps Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets.
(c) f is continuous and injective and E is Polish, so f maps Borel sets to Borel sets (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
(d) If Z ⊆ E is Hⁿ-null-measurable, there is a Borel Z₀ ⊆ Z with Hⁿ(Z ∖ Z₀) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq); then f(Z) = f(Z₀) ∪ f(Z ∖ Z₀) is a Borel set (c) union an Hⁿ-null set (b), hence Hⁿ-null-measurable.

2. Decomposition. For i ∈ ℕ let D_i := F_i(C_i) ∖ (N₀ ∪ ⋃_{j<i} F_j(C_j)). Each F_j(C_j) is compact (continuous image of the compact C_j), hence closed and Borel, and N₀ is Borel, so D_i is Borel. The D_i are pairwise disjoint (for j < i, D_i ∩ F_j(C_j) = ∅ and D_j ⊆ F_j(C_j)) and disjoint from N₀. Let M_i := M ∩ K ∩ D_i; these sets are Hⁿ-null-measurable (M is, K and D_i are Borel), pairwise disjoint and contained in M ∩ K. If x ∈ (M ∩ K) ∖ N₀, then x ∈ F_i(C_i) for some i by the covering hypothesis, and for the least such i, x ∈ D_i; hence M ∩ K = (M ∩ K ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_i M_i with Hⁿ(M ∩ K ∩ N₀) ≤ Hⁿ(N₀) = 0. Since f is injective, f(M ∩ K) = f(M ∩ K ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_i f(M_i), the sets f(M_i) are pairwise disjoint and Hⁿ-null-measurable (1(d)), and Hⁿ(f(M ∩ K ∩ N₀)) = 0 (1(b)). Set-lintegrals over sets that differ by an Hⁿ-null set coincide (setLIntegral_congr), and the lintegral over a countable union of pairwise disjoint null-measurable sets is the sum of the lintegrals (lintegral_iUnion₀). Therefore
imageMass a f K = Σ_i ∫⁻_{f(M_i)} u dHⁿ and ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)) dHⁿ = Σ_i ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)) dHⁿ,
and it suffices to prove, for every i,
(†) ∫⁻_{f(M_i)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)) dHⁿ(x).

3. The area formula on one piece. Fix i.
(a) Since M_i is Hⁿ-null-measurable there is a Borel A' ⊇ M_i with Hⁿ(A' ∖ M_i) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_superset_ae_eq); put A := A' ∩ D_i. Then A is Borel, M_i ⊆ A ⊆ D_i ⊆ F_i(C_i), and Hⁿ(A ∖ M_i) = 0.
(b) F_i is injective on C_i: if v, w ∈ C_i and F_i v = F_i w then c_i‖v − w‖ ≤ 0 with c_i > 0, so v = w. Let ψ_i := Function.invFunOn F_i C_i; then ψ_i(F_i v) = v for v ∈ C_i, and ψ_i(y) ∈ C_i, F_i(ψ_i y) = y for y ∈ F_i(C_i). Let B := C_i ∩ F_i⁻¹(A). B is Borel (C_i is compact hence closed, F_i is continuous), F_i(B) = A (because A ⊆ F_i(C_i)), and F_i is injective on B.
(c) G := f ∘ F_i is Lipschitz (constant L·L_i) and injective on B (f is injective). For v ∈ B ⊆ C_i, F_i is differentiable at v and f is differentiable at F_i(v), so fderiv ℝ G v = Df(F_i v) ∘ DF_i(v) (fderiv_comp). By LinearMap.normDet_comp, normDet(Λ ∘ A₀) = normDet(Λ restricted to range A₀)·normDet(A₀); hence, with T_i(v) := range DF_i(v),
JG(v) = J^{T_i(v)}(Df(F_i v))·JF_i(v), both factors ≥ 0.
(d) Define h: E → [0, ∞] by h(y) := ofReal(J^{T_i(ψ_i y)}(Df(y)))·ofReal(θ(y)) if y ∈ F_i(C_i), and h(y) := 0 otherwise. For v ∈ B we have F_i v ∈ F_i(C_i), ψ_i(F_i v) = v and u(G v) = ofReal(θ(F_i v)) (1(a)); since ofReal(αβ) = ofReal(α)·ofReal(β) for α ≥ 0,
ofReal(JG(v))·u(G v) = ofReal(JF_i(v))·h(F_i v).
(e) The weighted area formula for injective Lipschitz maps (SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, for any weight g: E → [0, ∞], measurable or not; here μHE[finrank ℝ ℝⁿ] = μHE[n] by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), applied to G on B with weight u and to F_i on B with weight h, gives
∫⁻_{f(A)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{G(B)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JG(v))·u(G v) dLⁿ(v) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JF_i(v))·h(F_i v) dLⁿ(v) = ∫⁻_{F_i(B)} h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_A h dHⁿ,
using G(B) = f(F_i(B)) = f(A) and (d).

4. From A back to M_i.
(a) Hⁿ(A ∖ M_i) = 0 and M_i ⊆ A give ∫⁻_A h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} h dHⁿ. Also f(M_i) ⊆ f(A) ⊆ f(M_i) ∪ f(A ∖ M_i) and Hⁿ(f(A ∖ M_i)) = 0 (1(b)), so ∫⁻_{f(A)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{f(M_i)} u dHⁿ.
(b) The tangent hypothesis holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, hence for Hⁿ⌞M_i-a.e. x since M_i ⊆ M (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). For such x ∈ M_i: x ∈ D_i ⊆ F_i(C_i), so w := ψ_i(x) ∈ C_i and F_i(w) = x, and the hypothesis gives T_x = range DF_i(w) = T_i(ψ_i x). Hence, by step 0 and since J ≥ 0,
h(x) = ofReal(J^{T_x}(Df(x)))·ofReal(θ(x)) = ofReal(θ(x)·J^{T_x}(Df(x))) = ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)).
Thus h = ofReal(θ·jac(Df, T)) Hⁿ⌞M_i-a.e., and ∫⁻_{M_i} h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)) dHⁿ(x) (lintegral_congr_ae).
(c) Combining 3(e), 4(a) and 4(b): ∫⁻_{f(M_i)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{f(A)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_A h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θ·jac(Df, T)) dHⁿ, which is (†).

5. Conclusion. Summing (†) over i ∈ ℕ and using step 2,
imageMass a f K = Σ_i ∫⁻_{f(M_i)} u dHⁿ = Σ_i ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θ·jac(Df, T)) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ(x)·jac(Df(x), T_x)) dHⁿ(x).
By definition jac(Df(x), T_x) = Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ ⟨Df(x)(p_{T_x}e_i), Df(x)(p_{T_x}e_j)⟩ + ⟨e_i − p_{T_x}e_i, e_j − p_{T_x}e_j⟩)) with p_{T_x} = ((mk a).tangentSpace x).starProjection, which is exactly the integrand of the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: jac(Λ, P) = normDet(Λ|_P): the bilinear form ⟨Λpu, Λpv⟩ + ⟨qu, qv⟩ is block diagonal (Gram of Λ on P, identity on P^⊥) in an orthonormal basis adapted to P ⊕ P^⊥; use normDet_sq_eq_det_gram and basis invariance of the determinant
f is injective and Lipschitz, so invFun f ∘ f = id and f maps Borel sets to Borel sets, Hⁿ-null sets to null sets and null-measurable sets to null-measurable sets
Disjointify the cover: M ∩ K = (M ∩ K ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃ M_i with M_i := M ∩ K ∩ D_i; both sides split into sums over i by lintegral_iUnion₀
On one piece: Borel A ⊇ M_i in D_i, B := C_i ∩ F_i⁻¹(A); the weighted area formula for f∘F_i and for F_i together with normDet_comp gives ∫⁻_{f(A)} u = ∫⁻_A h
Remove the null sets A ∖ M_i and f(A ∖ M_i) and identify h = ofReal(θ·jac(Df, T)) a.e. on M_i using the tangent hypothesis; then sum over i

subproblems.title: Derivative of the tangential Jacobian along a C¹ family of linear maps (Jacobi's formula; Simon Ch. 2, 5.2–5.3)
subproblems.statement: For all N ∈ ℕ and B ∈ ℝ there is C ∈ ℝ with the following property. Let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with standard basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, P ⊆ E a linear subspace with orthogonal projection p = P.starProjection and q = I − p, δ > 0, and Λ, Λ' : ℝ → L(E, E) with Λ(0) = I such that for every t ∈ (−δ, δ): Λ has derivative Λ'(t) at t, ‖Λ(t)‖ ≤ B, ‖Λ'(t)‖ ≤ B, and ‖v‖ ≤ B‖Λ(t)v‖ for all v ∈ E. Let J: ℝ → ℝ with J(t) = (det[⟨Λ(t)pe_i, Λ(t)pe_j⟩ + ⟨qe_i, qe_j⟩]_{i,j})^{1/2} for all t. Then for every t ∈ (−δ, δ): 0 ≤ J(t) ≤ C and J is differentiable at t with |J'(t)| ≤ C; and J has derivative trace(Λ'(0) ∘ p) at 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, steps 3.2–3.3 (Jacobi's formula; Simon Ch. 2, 5.2–5.3 and Ch. 4, 2.2), carried out on the N×N matrix S_P(Λ) of the parent's conventions, whose determinant is J^P(Λ)², instead of on the n×n Gram matrix of an orthonormal basis of P (the same determinant). Working with S_P removes the need for dim P = n and for a choice of basis of P. No errata apply.

Notation. E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N); e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N), an orthonormal basis of E (EuclideanSpace.basisFun); for ξ ∈ ℝ^N, |ξ|² := Σ_i ξ_i². p := P.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto P, q := I − p, so q v = v − p v. Standard facts used: p is self-adjoint and idempotent, ‖p v‖ ≤ ‖v‖, and q v ⊥ P; consequently ⟨p u, p v⟩ = ⟨p u, v⟩ = ⟨u, p v⟩, ⟨q u, q v⟩ = ⟨u, v⟩ − ⟨p u, p v⟩, ‖q v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ and ‖p v‖² + ‖q v‖² = ‖v‖². For t ∈ ℝ put
S(t) := [⟨Λ(t)p e_i, Λ(t)p e_j⟩ + ⟨q e_i, q e_j⟩]_{i,j ∈ Fin N},
so the hypothesis on J says J(t) = (det S(t))^{1/2} (Real.sqrt) for every t.

0. Choice of C. Let B₁ := max(B, 1) ≥ 1, M₀ := B₁² + 1, and
C := (N!·M₀^N)^{1/2} + N!·N·B₁^{N+2}·M₀^{N−1}
(N − 1 in ℕ; the second summand is 0 if N = 0). C depends only on N and B. Now fix P, Λ, Λ', J, δ satisfying the hypotheses, and let t ∈ (−δ, δ) unless stated otherwise. From the hypotheses, ‖Λ(t)‖ ≤ B ≤ B₁, ‖Λ'(t)‖ ≤ B₁, and ‖v‖ ≤ B‖Λ(t)v‖ ≤ B₁‖Λ(t)v‖ for all v (as ‖Λ(t)v‖ ≥ 0).

1. The quadratic form of S(t). S(t) is symmetric (the real inner product is symmetric). For ξ ∈ ℝ^N let v := Σ_i ξ_i e_i, so ‖v‖² = |ξ|². By bilinearity, Σ_{i,j} ξ_i S(t)_{ij} ξ_j = ‖Λ(t)(p v)‖² + ‖q v‖². Applying the lower bound to p v gives ‖Λ(t)(p v)‖² ≥ B₁^{−2}‖p v‖², and ‖q v‖² ≥ B₁^{−2}‖q v‖² because B₁ ≥ 1. Hence
ξᵀS(t)ξ ≥ B₁^{−2}(‖p v‖² + ‖q v‖²) = B₁^{−2}|ξ|².

2. Bounds for det S(t). (a) Lower bound: S(t) is real symmetric, so by the spectral theorem it has real eigenvalues λ_1, …, λ_N with an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, and det S(t) = Π_k λ_k (Matrix.IsHermitian.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues). For an eigenvector ξ ≠ 0 with eigenvalue λ, step 1 gives λ|ξ|² = ξᵀS(t)ξ ≥ B₁^{−2}|ξ|², so λ ≥ B₁^{−2}. Hence det S(t) ≥ B₁^{−2N} > 0. (b) Upper bound: |S(t)_{ij}| ≤ ‖Λ(t)‖²‖p e_i‖‖p e_j‖ + ‖q e_i‖‖q e_j‖ ≤ B₁² + 1 = M₀. By the Leibniz formula det S(t) = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin N)} sgn(σ) Π_k S(t)_{σ(k) k} (Matrix.det_apply), |det S(t)| ≤ N!·M₀^N.

3. Bound on J. J(t) = (det S(t))^{1/2} ≥ 0 and, by 2(b) and monotonicity of the square root, J(t) ≤ (N!·M₀^N)^{1/2} ≤ C.

4. Derivatives of the entries. Since Λ has derivative Λ'(t) at t and, for fixed w ∈ E, evaluation L ↦ L w is continuous linear, s ↦ Λ(s)w has derivative Λ'(t)w at t. By the product rule for the inner product (HasDerivAt.inner), s ↦ ⟨Λ(s)p e_i, Λ(s)p e_j⟩ has derivative ⟨Λ'(t)p e_i, Λ(t)p e_j⟩ + ⟨Λ(t)p e_i, Λ'(t)p e_j⟩ at t, and ⟨q e_i, q e_j⟩ does not depend on s. So each entry s ↦ S(s)_{ij} has derivative
S'(t)_{ij} := ⟨Λ'(t)p e_i, Λ(t)p e_j⟩ + ⟨Λ(t)p e_i, Λ'(t)p e_j⟩ at t, with |S'(t)_{ij}| ≤ 2B₁².

5. Derivative of det S. By the Leibniz formula, the product rule for finite products (HasDerivAt.finsetProd) and linearity, s ↦ det S(s) has derivative
D(t) := Σ_σ sgn(σ) Σ_k S'(t)_{σ(k) k} Π_{i ≠ k} S(t)_{σ(i) i}
at t. By 2(b) and step 4, |D(t)| ≤ N!·N·2B₁²·M₀^{N−1}.

6. Derivative of J and its bound. Since det S(t) > 0 (2(a)), HasDerivAt.sqrt gives that J = (s ↦ (det S(s))^{1/2}) has derivative d := D(t)/(2(det S(t))^{1/2}) at t. Using (det S(t))^{1/2} ≥ B₁^{−N} (2(a)),
|d| ≤ N!·N·2B₁²·M₀^{N−1}·B₁^N/2 = N!·N·B₁^{N+2}·M₀^{N−1} ≤ C.
Together with step 3 this proves the first conclusion: for every t ∈ (−δ, δ), 0 ≤ J(t) ≤ C and ∃ d, HasDerivAt J d t ∧ |d| ≤ C.

7. The value at t = 0. Note 0 ∈ (−δ, δ) since δ > 0. As Λ(0) = I, S(0)_{ij} = ⟨p e_i, p e_j⟩ + ⟨q e_i, q e_j⟩ = ⟨e_i, e_j⟩ = δ_{ij}, so S(0) = I, det S(0) = 1 and J(0) = 1. In D(0), Π_{i≠k} S(0)_{σ(i) i} = Π_{i≠k} δ_{σ(i) i} equals 1 if σ fixes every i ≠ k and 0 otherwise; a permutation fixing every i ≠ k also fixes k, so only σ = id contributes and D(0) = Σ_k S'(0)_{kk}. With L := Λ'(0) and Λ(0) = I, S'(0)_{kk} = ⟨L p e_k, p e_k⟩ + ⟨p e_k, L p e_k⟩ = 2⟨L p e_k, p e_k⟩. By step 6 at t = 0, J has derivative D(0)/(2·1) = Σ_k ⟨L p e_k, p e_k⟩ at 0.

8. Identification with the trace. By self-adjointness of p and symmetry of the real inner product, ⟨L p e_k, p e_k⟩ = ⟨e_k, (p ∘ L ∘ p) e_k⟩, so Σ_k ⟨L p e_k, p e_k⟩ = trace(p ∘ L ∘ p) (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun). By the cyclicity of the trace (LinearMap.trace_mul_comm with the factors p and L ∘ p) and p ∘ p = p, trace(p ∘ L ∘ p) = trace(L ∘ p ∘ p) = trace(L ∘ p). Hence J has derivative LinearMap.trace ℝ E ((Λ'(0)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ p.toLinearMap) at 0, which is the second conclusion. ∎

subproblems.title: Differentiation under the integral sign for θ-weighted Jacobian integrals over M ∩ K (Simon Ch. 4, 2.2)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, a = (M, θ) an admissible pair in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, V = v(M, θ) with weight μ_V, K ⊆ E compact, δ > 0, B ∈ ℝ, m: ℝ → [0, ∞], J, J': ℝ → E → ℝ and g: E → ℝ. Assume: for every t ∈ (−δ, δ), m(t) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ(x)J(t, x)) dHⁿ(x) and J(t, ·) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; g is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and g = 0 outside K; and for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x ∈ K: J'(0, x) = g(x) and, for all t ∈ (−δ, δ), 0 ≤ J(t, x) ≤ B, s ↦ J(s, x) has derivative J'(t, x) at t, and |J'(t, x)| ≤ B. Then t ↦ (m(t)).toReal has derivative ∫ g dμ_V at t = 0.

Source: the parent proof, step 4 ("Conclusion", 4.1–4.4: Simon Ch. 4, 2.2, differentiation under the integral sign), with the Jacobian J_t(x) replaced by an arbitrary function J satisfying the bounds established in the parent's steps 3.3–3.4. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ, Hⁿ := μHE[n], a = (M, θ) with IsRectifiablePair: M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K'. μ := (mk a).weight. Since K is compact it is closed, hence Borel. Let ν := Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) = (μHE[n]).restrict (a.M ∩ K), and I := (−δ, δ), an open neighbourhood of 0 (δ > 0).

1. Preliminaries on ν.
(a) θ is ν-integrable (IsRectifiablePair.locallyIntegrable applied to K); in particular θ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable.
(b) M ∩ K is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so ν-a.e. x lies in M ∩ K (ae_restrict_mem₀); hence θ(x) > 0 for ν-a.e. x.
(c) ν = (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K (Measure.restrict_restrict, K measurable, and K ∩ M = M ∩ K). Hence a statement of the form "for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, x ∈ K → R(x)" implies "for ν-a.e. x, R(x)" (ae_restrict_iff', or ae_restrict_of_ae with the implication). Applied to the pointwise hypothesis: for ν-a.e. x, J'(0, x) = g(x) and, for all t ∈ I, 0 ≤ J(t, x) ≤ B, s ↦ J(s, x) has derivative J'(t, x) at t, and |J'(t, x)| ≤ B.
(d) ν ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono on M ∩ K ⊆ M), so every function that is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure). This applies to J(t, ·) for t ∈ I and to g.

2. The integrands. For t ∈ I let F(t, x) := θ(x)·J(t, x) and F'(t, x) := θ(x)·J'(t, x). By 1(a), 1(d), F(t, ·) is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (product). By 1(b), 1(c), for ν-a.e. x: 0 ≤ F(t, x) ≤ B·θ(x) for all t ∈ I. Since B·θ is ν-integrable, F(t, ·) is ν-integrable (Integrable.mono' with the bound B·θ). As F(t, ·) ≥ 0 ν-a.e.,
m(t) = ∫⁻ ofReal(F(t, x)) dν(x) = ofReal(∫ F(t, x) dν(x)) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal),
and since ∫ F(t, ·) dν ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg_of_ae), (m t).toReal = ∫ F(t, x) dν(x) for every t ∈ I (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).

3. Differentiation under the integral sign. Apply hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le with x₀ := 0, the neighbourhood s := I of 0, the functions F, F', and bound(x) := B·θ(x):
– for every t in the neighbourhood I of 0, F(t, ·) is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (step 2);
– F(0, ·) is ν-integrable (step 2 with t = 0);
– F'(0, ·) is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: by 1(c), F'(0, x) = θ(x)·g(x) for ν-a.e. x, and θ·g is ν-a.e. strongly measurable by 1(a), 1(d) (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr);
– for ν-a.e. x and all t ∈ I: |F'(t, x)| = θ(x)·|J'(t, x)| ≤ B·θ(x) (θ(x) > 0 by 1(b), bound by 1(c));
– bound = B·θ is ν-integrable (1(a));
– for ν-a.e. x and all t ∈ I: s ↦ F(s, x) = θ(x)·J(s, x) has derivative θ(x)·J'(t, x) = F'(t, x) at t (HasDerivAt.const_mul and 1(c)).
The lemma gives HasDerivAt (t ↦ ∫ F(t, x) dν(x)) (∫ F'(0, x) dν(x)) 0.

4. The derivative value. By 1(c), F'(0, ·) = θ·g ν-a.e., so ∫ F'(0, x) dν = ∫ θ(x)g(x) dν(x) (integral_congr_ae). Now compute ∫ g dμ. By definition of the weight on the class mk a, μ = pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ρ) with ρ(x) := ofReal(θ(x)) (Quot.lift on Quot.mk reduces definitionally). Since g = 0 off K, ∫ g dμ = ∫_K g dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). Further μ⌞K = ((Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K).withDensity(ρ) = ν.withDensity(ρ) (restrict_withDensity, K measurable, and 1(c)). The density ρ is ν-a.e. measurable (θ is, by 1(a); ENNReal.ofReal is measurable) and ρ(x) < ∞ for all x, so integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ (no integrability of g is needed) gives
∫_K g dμ = ∫ (ofReal θ(x)).toReal·g(x) dν(x) = ∫ θ(x)g(x) dν(x),
because (ofReal θ(x)).toReal = θ(x) whenever θ(x) ≥ 0, which holds ν-a.e. by 1(b). Hence ∫ F'(0, x) dν = ∫ g dμ.

5. Conclusion. By step 2 the functions t ↦ (m t).toReal and t ↦ ∫ F(t, x) dν(x) agree on the neighbourhood I of 0, so by step 3, step 4 and HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq,
HasDerivAt (t ↦ (m t).toReal) (∫ g dμ) 0, i.e. HasDerivAt (fun t ↦ (m t).toReal) (∫ x, g x ∂(mk a).weight) 0. ∎
